Compare habitat connectivity of a scenario against a baseline

Source: R/habitat-connectivity-comparison.R
habitat_connectivity_comparison.Rd

Starts from habitat and barrier layers, rather than the connectivity objects compare_connectivity() takes. Give it the baseline's habitat and barrier, and the layers a planned change replaces, and it runs the full connectivity pipeline (via habitat_connectivity()) on the baseline and on the scenario and compares them. interpatch_distance may be a vector, in which case the comparison is run once per distance and the per-distance results are stacked.

Usage

habitat_connectivity_comparison(
  habitat_baseline,
  barrier_baseline,
  species,
  interpatch_distance,
  habitat_scenario = NULL,
  barrier_scenario = NULL,
  scenario_name = NULL,
  directions = 4,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

habitat_baseline

Terra SpatRaster. The baseline habitat layer: the landscape as it is today.

barrier_baseline

Terra SpatRaster. The baseline barrier layer.

species

Species name. E.g., "Superb Fairy Wren".

interpatch_distance

Numeric. The distance (in metres) at which habitat patches are considered connected. May be a scalar or a vector; a vector runs the comparison once per distance. See habitat_connectivity().

habitat_scenario

Terra SpatRaster, or NULL. The whole habitat layer after the planned change, on the same grid as habitat_baseline.

barrier_scenario

Terra SpatRaster, or NULL. The whole barrier layer after the planned change, on the same grid as barrier_baseline.

scenario_name

Character. An optional label for the scenario, for example "Bentley Project". Passed to compare_connectivity(), and appears in the scenario_name column on every row. Defaults to NULL, which gives NA.

directions

Which neighbouring raster cells join into one patch, passed to terra::patches(). 4, the default, is the rook's case: cells join only through a shared edge. 8 is the queen's case: cells that touch only at a corner join as well. It applies to rasters only, not to sf_habitat_connectivity().

verbose

Logical. Display progress messages (default: TRUE).

Value

A compare_connectivity object: a tibble with four rows (baseline, scenario, change, pct_change) per interpatch distance. A scalar interpatch_distance gives four rows; a length-3 vector gives twelve rows (four per distance). See compare_connectivity() for the columns.

Details

A scenario is the landscape after a planned change. Give the layers the plan changes, and the function takes the rest from the baseline:

You giveThe scenario's habitatThe scenario's barrier
habitat_scenariohabitat_scenariobarrier_baseline
barrier_scenariohabitat_baselinebarrier_scenario
bothhabitat_scenariobarrier_scenario

Each layer you give must be the whole layer after the change, not just the part that changes: a barrier scenario holding only a new road drops every existing road. If you give both, the comparison shows their combined effect, not how much came from each; to see each one's share, run it again with one layer at a time. The shares won't add up exactly, because changes interact: a new road beside new habitat matters more than either alone.

A scenario layer must be on the same grid as the layer it replaces, or this gives an error: put it there with onto_grid(). A scenario identical to the baseline gives a warning, since every change value will be zero.

This runs the full connectivity pipeline 2 * length(interpatch_distance) times (buffering is the slow step), so a long vector of distances will take proportionally longer.

See also

habitat_connectivity_scenarios() for several scenarios at once, compare_connectivity(), habitat_connectivity(), and vignette("scenario-comparison").

Examples

# \donttest{
# a scenario that changes the barrier: the habitat stays as it is today
habitat_connectivity_comparison(
  habitat_baseline = example_wren_habitat(),
  barrier_baseline = example_wren_barrier(),
  species = "Superb Fairy Wren",
  interpatch_distance = 200,
  barrier_scenario = example_wren_barrier_scenario(),
  verbose = FALSE
)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 10
#>   scenario_name measure  species interpatch_distance n_patches effective_mesh_ha
#>   <chr>         <chr>    <chr>                 <dbl>     <dbl>             <dbl>
#> 1 NA            baseline Superb…                 200   282               334.   
#> 2 NA            scenario Superb…                 200   283               333.   
#> 3 NA            change   Superb…                 200     1                -0.965
#> 4 NA            pct_cha… Superb…                 200     0.355            -0.289
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: prob_connectedness <dbl>, patch_area_mean <dbl>,
#> #   patch_area_total_ha <dbl>, data_resolution <chr>
# }
